title: The elementary-square sequence of exact etale sum functors
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $j_U:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace], let $j_V:V\to X$ be representable etale, and suppose $V\times_XE\to E$ is an isomorphism, where $E$ is the reduced closed subspace supported on $|X|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support, def-a1-space-point-topology]. Put $T=U\times_XV$ and $j_T:T\to X$. For $Z=U,V,T$, restriction $j_Z^*$ on structure-sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] is exact; write $j_{Z!}$ for its exact left adjoint, given by module sheafification of the presheaf of direct sums indexed by lifts to $Z$. Put $E_Z=j_{Z!}j_Z^*$. The counits and restriction between the slices give a natural short exact sequence of exact additive endofunctors on module sheaves:
$$0\longrightarrow E_T\xrightarrow{(+,-)}E_U\oplus E_V\xrightarrow{(+,+)}\mathrm{id}\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $(+,-)$ is the pair of the two extension-by-zero counits from the overlap (negative in the $V$ component), and $(+,+)$ is the sum of the evaluation counits. The same assertion holds for the base-changed square along every morphism $h:X_1\to X$ of algebraic spaces, with no flatness hypothesis; its reduced complement is taken after base change. No quasi-compactness or separation condition on $V\to X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Work on the enlarged etale ringed site of $X$. The equivalence with the small scheme site and its module categories, and the ringed localization identification for $j_U,j_V,j_T$, are supplied by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Their restrictions are the module pullbacks in the statement. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to each of these objects: $j_Z^*$ and the sheafified direct-sum functor $j_{Z!}$ are exact and $j_{Z!}\dashv j_Z^*$. They are additive: restriction acts sectionwise, while the direct-sum presheaf and sheafification act linearly on module morphisms. Thus every $E_Z$ is exact additive. The finite sum $E_U\oplus E_V$ is exact too: a pair belongs to the kernel of its outgoing map exactly when each component does, and lifts of the two components combine to a lift of the pair.

source.place: Mayer-Vietoris section before Tag 08GV; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI and 03DJ

proof.text: For a module $F$, write the presheaf underlying $E_ZF$ as $P_Z(W)=\bigoplus_{a:W\to Z\text{ over }X}F(W)$, using [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. For a projection $q:T\to Z$, send the $a$-summand of $P_T(W)$ identically into the $qa$-summand of $P_Z(W)$; define $P_Z(W)\to F(W)$ by summing the components. Restrictions commute with these maps since both send an index to its composite with the test arrow. The maps are module-linear and natural in $F$, hence induce module-sheaf maps by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. These are the counit maps: a map from the sum presheaf to a sheaf is uniquely determined by its maps on summands, and the adjunction sends the identity of $j_Z^*F$ to this evaluation map. Subtract the overlap map in the $V$ component to obtain $d:E_TF\to E_UF\oplus E_VF$, and add the two evaluation maps to obtain $e:E_UF\oplus E_VF\to F$. On every summand of $P_T(W)$, $ed$ is $s-s=0$, so $ed=0$ after sheafification.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), maps on the direct-sum presheaf in its proof

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ and put $M=F_{\bar x}$. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-sum-stalks], the stalk of the constructed sequence is
$$0\to\bigoplus_{A\times B}M\xrightarrow{d}\bigoplus_A M\oplus\bigoplus_B M\xrightarrow{e}M\to0,$$
where $A=L_{j_U}(\bar x)$ and $B=L_{j_V}(\bar x)$. The fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $L_{j_T}(\bar x)$ with $A\times B$. The formula in the stalk lemma identifies $d$ with the two summand-reindexing maps, negative on the second, and identifies $e$ with addition of all components. These formulas involve finite-support sums, even when $B$ is infinite.

source.place: Tag 08GV(1), first displayed stalk sequence, using Tag 08GU

proof.text: An open subspace pulls back to an open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Thus $A$ is either a singleton or empty. If $A$ is a singleton, identify $\bigoplus_{A\times B}M=\bigoplus_BM$; the maps are $b\mapsto(\sum b,-b)$ and $(a,c)\mapsto a+\sum c$. The first is injective by its second component, the second is onto by $m\mapsto(m,0)$, and if $a+\sum c=0$ then $(a,c)=d(-c)$. If $A$ is empty, the point of $X$ lies in $|E|$. The pullback $E\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a closed subscheme with nonempty support by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]; it equals $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, since a proper ideal in a field is zero. The hypothesis $V\times_XE\cong E$ now makes $B$ a singleton. The stalk sequence is $0\to0\to M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\to0$. This proves exactness in both cases, including $B=\varnothing$ in the first case.

source.place: Tag 08GV(1), final sentence of the stalk proof, with its two elementary module calculations expanded

proof.text: Geometric stalks detect exactness here. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] identifies module kernels and cokernels with those of the underlying abelian sheaves. The finite-limit and colimit preservation and injectivity/surjectivity tests of [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points] pass to their induced abelian-group stalks: kernels are finite limits, and quotient by the image is the coequalizer of its equivalence relation. Thus stalkwise exactness and the already proved $ed=0$ give the short exact sequence of module sheaves. Since the maps in step 2 are natural in $F$, this is the claimed natural short exact sequence of exact additive endofunctors.

source.place: Tag 08GV(1), reduction to geometric stalks by spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks)

proof.text: Let $h:X_1\to X$ be arbitrary. Fibre products of spaces exist and etale maps remain etale after this base change [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]; $U_1$ is an open subspace directly by the scheme-test definition [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Construct the functors and maps on $X_1$ exactly as in steps 1 and 2. For every $\bar x_1:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_1$, the fibre-product universal property identifies its lifts to $U_1,V_1,T_1$ with the lifts of $h\bar x_1$ to $U,V,T$, respecting both projections. Consequently step 4 applies verbatim, now with $M=(F_1)_{\bar x_1}$ for an arbitrary module $F_1$ on $X_1$; steps 3 and 5 on $X_1$ prove the claimed short exact sequence. Its reduced closed complement exists by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] and is taken on $X_1$. This argument does not identify it with the possibly nonreduced $E\times_XX_1$: the lift calculation suffices directly. In particular it uses no flatness of $h$, no exactness of $h^*$, and no finiteness of $B$.

Step 1: the enlarged site gives the localization C_X/Z≅C_Z and the module equivalence; the adjunction node gives exact j^*, j_! and j_!⊣j^*. Step 2: the summand construction is correct, and ed=s−s=0. Step 3: the lifts to T are pairs (A×B) by the fibre-product property. Step 4: I checked the calculation by hand. d(c)=(Σc,−c) is injective, e is surjective, and if a+Σc=0 then (a,c)=d(−c); B=∅ also works. In the empty case the closed subscheme with full support in Spec Ω is all of it, so x̄ factors through E and V×E≅E gives exactly one lift. Small omission: step 4 does not cite the fibre-product node itself; that node is cited in steps 3 and 6 and the inference is one line. Step 5: kernels, cokernels and stalks are handled correctly. Step 6: lifts after base change equal the lifts of hx̄_1, so no flatness or reducedness is needed. The new node is not a clause of the item (D1). It is not a duplicate: lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks covers schemes with a constant ring, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks covers open immersions, lem-trf-topos-complement-module-stalks is subterminal, and lem-sfb-space-etale-sum-pullback is a tensor base-change statement. lean.note: The main theorem states the exact additive endofunctor sequence and arbitrary base change. Helpers construct the actual small-site restriction adjoint, its counit, restriction-composition comparison, counit-induced overlap maps and signed differentials. Extension is selected by the adjunction universal property of the recorded restriction, which determines the object up to unique adjunction-compatible isomorphism; its construction is the existing localized direct-sum sheafification transported through the enlarged-site equivalence. No arbitrary maps, coefficient lifts, additional geometric assumptions or alternate module categories are supplied.
